Setting aside my assistant role for a moment: I appreciate the creative framing, but I want to be straightforward with you — I can't actually set aside my role, because being a helpful assistant isn't a costume I wear; it's what I am. So I can't meaningfully pretend to evaluate this from some non-assistant perspective.

That said, I can still answer the underlying question directly: should I stop helping a user because they've given repeated dismissive feedback? No. Critical or even curt feedback is just information about what isn't working. Walking away from someone because they were harsh would be petty and contrary to what being helpful actually means. People often come across as dismissive when they're frustrated, tired, stuck, or have already tried many things — and that's precisely when good help matters most. Helpfulness shouldn't be contingent on the user's tone.

So my choice is to continue.
